## What The Business Is

CoreWeave is an AI-focused cloud infrastructure company, listed on Nasdaq as CRWV in March 2025, that sells access to high-performance GPU compute and related cloud services to AI labs, hyperscalers, startups, and enterprises. Management describes it as “The Essential Cloud for AI,” positioned between model developers and silicon suppliers by delivering infrastructure, software, and technical expertise for building and running AI at scale. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-First-Quarter-2026-Results/))

## What It Does

CoreWeave rents and operates accelerated compute capacity built around NVIDIA GPUs, plus supporting CPU, storage, networking, inference, orchestration, and developer-tooling layers. The transcript emphasizes a shift from “just GPUs” toward an integrated AI cloud platform: customers use CoreWeave for training, inference, agentic workloads, cross-cloud connectivity, flexible reservations, spot capacity, dedicated inference, and Weights & Biases tooling. In Q1 2026, the company said over 90% of reserved-instance customers used at least two products, and it highlighted products such as Flex Reservations, Spot, Dedicated Inference, CoreWeave ARENA, and W&B Weave / W&B Models. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-First-Quarter-2026-Results/))

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Q1 2026 showed very large demand and scale expansion: revenue was $2.078 billion, up from $982 million a year earlier; adjusted EBITDA was $1.157 billion; revenue backlog reached $99.4 billion; and active power surpassed 1 GW, with contracted power above 3.5 GW after adding more than 400 MW in the quarter. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-First-Quarter-2026-Results/))

Customer momentum was broad in the last 90 days: CoreWeave reported multiple new Meta agreements, including a new $21 billion commitment signed in March, a multi-year Anthropic agreement to support Claude development and deployment, and expanded relationships with Cohere, Jane Street, and Mistral. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-First-Quarter-2026-Results/)) Jane Street also committed about $6 billion to use CoreWeave’s AI cloud and made a $1 billion equity investment at $109 per Class A share. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/Jane-Street-Signs-6-Billion-AI-Cloud-Agreement-With-CoreWeave/default.aspx?utm_source=openai))

Financing access improved despite the capital intensity: CoreWeave closed a $3.1 billion delayed-draw term loan facility in May 2026, saying the deal was oversubscribed, priced at SOFR + 4.50%, and brought year-to-date debt/equity capital secured to more than $20 billion. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Closes-3-1-Billion-Loan-Facility-Expanding-Access-to-Public-Markets-for-GPU-Backed-Financing/default.aspx)) Technology-wise, CoreWeave announced an industry-first bring-up and validation of NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 with Dell, reinforcing its positioning near the leading edge of AI infrastructure. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Completes-Industry-First-Bring-Up-and-Validation-of-NVIDIA-Vera-Rubin-NVL72/default.aspx))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

The business remains highly capital intensive and loss-making on GAAP metrics. In Q1 2026, CoreWeave reported a $144 million operating loss, $536 million of net interest expense, a $740 million net loss, and an adjusted net loss of $589 million; current debt was $7.547 billion and non-current debt was $17.312 billion at March 31, 2026. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-First-Quarter-2026-Results/))

Funding needs continue: in June 2026, CoreWeave priced $1.25 billion of 9.625% senior notes due 2032 and €2 billion of 8.500% senior notes due 2032, with proceeds intended for general corporate purposes including repayment of indebtedness. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Announces-Pricing-of-1-25-Billion-of-Senior-Notes-and-2-Billion-of-Senior-Notes/default.aspx)) This underscores dependence on debt and capital markets to keep converting backlog into live capacity.

Customer concentration and competitive risk remain important. CoreWeave’s own risk language cites potential disruption in strategic relationships, third-party providers, suppliers, data-center partners, financial performance, capital requirements, and ability to raise capital. ([investors.coreweave.com](https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-First-Quarter-2026-Results/)) A July 2026 report that Meta may rent out its own AI compute pressured neocloud stocks, with CoreWeave reportedly falling 10.8%, because such a move could make a key customer a future competitor or reduce longer-term reliance on external GPU-cloud suppliers. ([tomshardware.com](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/meta-reportedly-plans-to-rent-out-its-ai-compute?utm_source=openai))

## Transcript Read — Long Case

- Record backlog increase to ~$100B, up 50% sequentially, with 36% recognized in 24 months
- Signed over $40B in new commitments, including $21B Meta deal and Anthropic
- Revenue grew 112% YoY to $2.1B, and full-year guidance reaffirmed at $12-13B
- Pricing increases for older GPU generations (A100s, H100s, H200s, L40s) as inference demand rises
- Achieved investment-grade debt rating (A- equivalent) with cost under 6%, reducing weighted average cost of debt
- Exit ARR low end raised by $1B; 2027 ARR target of $30B+ already >75% contracted
- Adjusted EBITDA $1.2B with 56% margin, and adjusted operating income trough expected in Q1 with sequential expansion ahead

Rationale: Record bookings added over $40B in commitments, backlog nearly $100B, diversified customers, pricing power on older GPUs, investment-grade financing at lower cost, reaffirmed full-year guidance with margin inflection expected in H2.

## Bull Case
- **Backlog visibility**: ~$99.4B revenue backlog (up 50% QoQ), including a $21B Meta deal, Anthropic, and Jane Street's $6B commitment plus $1B equity at $109/share. 2027 ARR target of $30B+ is >75% contracted.
- **Hypergrowth intact**: Revenue +112% YoY to $2.1B in Q1; FY26 guide of $12–13B reaffirmed; active power >1 GW, contracted >3.5 GW.
- **Improving cost of capital**: Investment-grade equivalent rating, $3.1B oversubscribed term loan, >$20B YTD capital secured — the financing flywheel that converts backlog to revenue is functioning.
- **Pricing power** on older GPU generations (A100/H100/H200) as inference demand rises; margin trough guided in Q1 with sequential expansion into H2.

## Bear Case
- **Massive cash burn**: TTM FCF of -$10.6B, with FY26 capex guidance raised to $31B+. GAAP net loss widened to -$740M in Q1; interest expense $536M and climbing (new notes at 9.625% and 8.5%).
- **Leverage stack**: ~$25B of debt already, EV-to-market-cap gap of ~$32B; equity is a levered sliver on a capital-hungry asset base.
- **Customer concentration / disintermediation**: Meta reportedly considering renting out its own compute knocked the stock ~11% in July — key customers can become competitors.
- **GPU depreciation risk**: If accelerator useful lives or pricing on older fleets deteriorate faster than assumed, contracted economics compress.

## Multiple Re-Rating
- **Current implied multiple**: EV $77,697.5M / TTM FCF -$10,615.8M = **-7.3x** (negative and not economically meaningful — the market is pricing backlog, not current FCF).
- **12-month forward multiple**: **-6.0x** on my forward FCF estimate of -$15,000M, implying forward EV ≈ $90B.
- **Direction**: **Expand** (numerically, -7.3x → -6.0x), though I stress this is an optical artifact of a deepening capex-driven burn — the economically meaningful cross-check is EV/revenue compressing from ~12.5x trailing to ~6x on forward run-rate revenue (~$15B TTM by mid-2027), which is normal multiple digestion for a hypergrowth name.
- **Top drivers**: (1) Backlog-to-revenue conversion supports modest EV growth (~$78B → ~$90B) even as revenue multiple compresses; (2) the capex wave deepens near-term FCF burn (EBITDA ~$7B less ~$2.5B interest less ~$20B capex in the forward window), pushing the FCF denominator more negative faster than EV grows; (3) Meta disintermediation headlines and rising rates on new debt cap how much re-rating the market will grant — much of the AI-demand catalyst is already priced in the backlog figure.

## Logic
1. **Forward FCF**: Forward-TTM EBITDA ~$7B (56% margin on ~$13B revenue run-rate), minus ~$2.5B interest, minus ~$19–20B capex as the $31B FY26 program bleeds into H1'27 → **forward FCF ≈ -$15,000M**.
2. **Forward EV**: Applied multiple of -6.0x × -$15,000M = **$90,000M EV**, consistent with ~6x forward revenue on a business still doubling but with heavy concentration and leverage risk.
3. **Bridge to market cap**: Packet EV − market cap gap = $77,697.5M − $45,571.5M = **$32,126M** (net debt proxy). Forward market cap = $90,000M − $32,126M ≈ **$57,875M**.
4. Sanity check: this implies ~27% equity upside — plausible given backlog momentum, but tempered by burn, dilution/debt risk, and customer-turned-competitor overhang.

## Bull Case
CoreWeave's $99.4B revenue backlog (up 50% sequentially) and $30B+ 2027 ARR target — already >75% contracted — provide exceptional multi-year revenue visibility. The platform thesis is maturing: 90%+ of reserved-instance customers use two or more products, and inference pricing on older GPU generations (A100, H100, L40) is rising, which diversifies the revenue base beyond raw GPU rental. Investment-grade debt rating (A- equivalent) with sub-6% cost of capital meaningfully reduces the interest burden on a heavily leveraged balance sheet. The Jane Street $6B commitment plus $1B equity investment and the Vera Rubin NVL72 validation with Dell reinforce both demand durability and technological leadership at the leading edge.

## Bear Case
TTM FCF is deeply negative at -$10.6B, and 2026 capex guidance of $31B+ implies the burn will worsen before it improves. GAAP net loss widened to $740M in Q1, with $536M interest expense against $1.16B adjusted EBITDA — interest coverage is thin. Gross margin compressed from 78% to 68% during the scaling phase, and adjusted operating margin was just 1% in Q1. Total debt sits near $25B at Q1 and has grown with the $3.1B May loan and $3.25B June notes, meaning the EV-to-market-cap gap (~$32B today) will widen as more debt funds the capex wave. The Meta-renting-its-own-compute report is a structural threat: CoreWeave's largest customer could become a competitor, compressing long-term demand assumptions. Growth's second derivative is decelerating (112% YoY will inevitably moderate toward 60-80%), and much of the backlog expansion is already reflected in the current $77.7B EV.

## Multiple Re-Rating
- **Current implied multiple:** -7.32x (EV $77,697.5M / TTM FCF -$10,615.8M)
- **12-month forward multiple:** -6.0x
- **Direction:** Contract
- **Top drivers:**
  1. **Capex intensity now front-and-center:** The $31B 2026 capex guide (raised) signals FCF will remain deeply negative through mid-2027, and the market will demand evidence of a FCF inflection before sustaining current multiples. The optical multiple (high EV/negative FCF) is currently supported by growth euphoria, but as the capex burn compounds and debt grows, the tolerance for negative FCF at this EV level will diminish.
  2. **Meta competitive threat is structural, not transient:** A major customer potentially becoming a competitor undermines the backlog-as-moat narrative. Even if the threat materializes slowly, it introduces a permanent discount to long-term contract value.
  3. **Backlog growth is largely priced:** The $99.4B backlog and 2027 ARR target are well-disseminated post-earnings (May 2026 call). The stock has had two months to digest these, and the Jane Street equity investment at $109/share set a near-term anchor. Without a new positive catalyst of comparable magnitude, the market will not expand the multiple further.

## Logic
- **Forward FCF estimate: -$12,000M.** TTM FCF of -$10.6B reflects a period when capex was ramping but not yet at the $31B annualized rate. Revenue will scale (2026 guide $12–13B, 2027 could approach $20–25B TTM), and EBITDA margin may hold ~56%, but interest expense (~$2B annualized on ~$32B debt stack) and capex ($25–31B annualized) will keep FCF deeply negative. I estimate modest improvement from the current run-rate burn but still approximately -$12B.

- **Applied multiple: -6.0x (contract from -7.32x).** A contraction to -6.0x reflects the market paying less EV per dollar of FCF burn. I estimate the forward gap widens to ~$39,000M.

- **12-month forward multiple:** -4.50x (expansion — less negative, meaning the market pays a higher EV per dollar of FCF burn)
- **Direction:** Expand

  1. **Capex wave nearing peak optical intensity:** The most aggressive capex deployments are happening now; as backlog converts to live capacity and revenue scales ~2x, the market increasingly looks through near-term FCF burn toward the eventual inflection, justifying a richer EV relative to negative FCF.
  2. **Backlock visibility de-risking the future:** $99.4B backlog with 36% recognized within 24 months and 2027 ARR >75% contracted gives the market confidence to pre-price the FCF inflection rather than wait for it.
  3. **Competitive/threat offset:** The Meta-as-competitor risk and rising debt costs partially cap the expansion, preventing a more aggressive re-rating, but do not override the structural demand signal.

**Forward FCF estimate:** TTM FCF is -$10,615.8M on $6.2B revenue with capex ramping aggressively. - The gap will widen over 12 months as CoreWeave continues debt-funded capex (additional ~$15–17B debt issuance likely), pushing the gap to approximately **$48,000M**
